blocks.title: Core Concepts
blocks.text:
Hydrocarbons are organic compounds composed entirely of hydrogen and carbon atoms.

Classification is based on bonding and structure:

  • Alkanes: Saturated hydrocarbons with single bonds.
  • Alkenes: Unsaturated hydrocarbons with one double bond.
  • Alkynes: Unsaturated hydrocarbons with one triple bond.
  • Aromatic hydrocarbons: Characterized by delocalized pi electrons and follow Huckel's rule.

blocks.title: Formulas & Mathematical Relations
blocks.text:

C_nH_{2n} \quad \text{(Alkenes)} \\
C_nH_{2n-2} \quad \text{(Alkynes)} \\
C_nH_n \quad \text{(Aromatic hydrocarbons - Monocyclic)}$  • Conditions: These formulas assume a single hydrocarbon chain without rings or additional functional groups.

blocks.title: Preparation of Alkane
blocks.text:
• Wurtz Reaction:

$2R-X + 2Na \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} R-R + 2NaX$• From Carboxylic Acids

Kolbe's Electrolysis

  • On electrolysis of sodium/potassium salt of carboxylic acid, generally, alkane is obtained as a product.
Points to Remember:

Due to the increase in concentration of OH, the pH of the solution increases with time during electrolysis.

$CH_4$ cannot be prepared.

$H_2$ gas is released at the cathode, and $CO_2$ gas is released at the anode.$$

Decarboxylation of Carboxylic Acids:

Carboxylic acid or sodium salts of carboxylic acids are heated with soda-lime.

$CH_3COONa + NaOH \xrightarrow{\Delta, \text{soda lime}} CH_4 + Na_2CO_3$Limitations: Not applicable for tertiary acids.

blocks.answer: The given compound is 1,2-dibromocyclohexane. When this compound is treated with zinc dust and heat, a dehalogenation reaction occurs. Zinc reduces the two bromine atoms (Br) and eliminates them as ZnBr₂, forming an alkene (cyclohexene) from which the bromine atoms are removed.

blocks.title: Example 2
blocks.question:
Acidic dehydration of alcohol involves :-

(1) E1 elimination

(2) Carbocation rearrangement if possible

(3) Saytzeff's product is formed as major product

(4) All
blocks.answer:
Correct Answer: (4) All

  • E1 elimination: The reaction proceeds via the E1 mechanism, especially for secondary and tertiary alcohols.
  • Carbocation rearrangement: If a more stable carbocation can form, rearrangement occurs.
  • Saytzeff's product: The major product is the more substituted alkene (Saytzeff's rule).
Thus, all the given statements are correct.
options: (3) Saytzeff's product is formed as major product

blocks.title: CORE CONCEPTS
blocks.text: Characteristic reaction of alkene is Electrophilic Addition Reactions (EAR)

blocks.title: Markovnikov's Rule
blocks.text:
The Markovnikov's rule states that negative part of the reagent gets attached to that carbon of double bond which possesses a lesser number of hydrogen atoms.

Note-

• Markovnikov’s rule is not applicable if alkene is symmetrical.

blocks.title: Reaction with X2/CCl4
blocks.text:
• Electrophile contains lone pair.
  • No carbocation intermediate is formed so no rearrangement is possible.
  • Reaction intermediate: Cyclic halonium ion.
Test of Unsaturation

Unknown organic compound $\xrightarrow[CCl_4]{Br_2}$ Reddish brown color disappears  $\rightarrow$ Unsaturation may be present.

blocks.title: Hydroboration Oxidation (HBO)
blocks.text:
Hydroboration Oxidation (HBO)

Points to remember

• In this reaction, the addition of water takes place by anti-Markovnikov addition, and water and alcohol are formed.
    • No carbocation intermediate is formed, so no rearrangement takes place.

modules.name: Reactions of Aromatic Hydrocarbon and its Derivatives

blocks.title: CORE CONCEPTS
blocks.text:
• Benzene derivatives undergo electrophilic substitution reactions, maintaining the aromatic ring structure.

  • Common reactions include nitration, sulfonation, halogenation, Friedel-Crafts alkylation, and acylation.

blocks.title: Points to Remember (ESR)
blocks.text:
• Rate towards ESR $\propto$ Nucleophilicity of benzene ring $\propto$ stability of  $\sigma$ complex
    • Exceptions-

• Halogens are weakly deactivating but ortho para directing.

modules.name: environmental and hazardous impact on human health

blocks.title: CORE CONCEPTS
blocks.text: • Certain hydrocarbons are toxic, causing respiratory problems and potentially being carcinogenic.

blocks.title: FORMULAS & MATHEMATICAL RELATIONS
blocks.text:
• Combustion Reaction of Hydrocarbons:
$C_xH_y + \left(x + \frac{y}{4}\right)O_2 \rightarrow xCO_2 + \frac{y}{2}H_2O$
  • Assumes complete combustion, ideal conditions, and stoichiometric oxygen supply.

blocks.title: COMMON MISTAKES
blocks.text:
• Confusing complete and incomplete combustion: Complete combustion produces CO₂; incomplete combustion produces CO and other pollutants.
  • Assuming all hydrocarbons are equally harmful; aromatic hydrocarbons are generally more hazardous.
